stories.title: iFixit teardown finds Apple HomeView difficult to repair
stories.summary: iFixit expected the new HomeView hub to be as repairable as recent iPads and HomePods. Instead, the team reported snapping components and applying excessive force to the logic board during disassembly. Apple appears to have moved away from its recent focus on designing for repairability.

stories.title: Solar canopy added to electric houseboat concept
stories.summary: Albatross Marine Design has unveiled OASIS, a 66-foot electric houseboat concept featuring a solar canopy. The design includes a private living level and a social deck. The studio, led by Albert Nazarov, received recognition for the project at the 2026 European Product Design Award.

stories.title: Framework opens preorders for wireless keyboard
stories.summary: Framework has opened preorders for its Wireless Touchpad Keyboard at $99, requiring a $50 deposit. The company aims to provide a better experience than the $35 Logitech K400. The keyboard is intended for use on a couch, though it carries a higher price point than the competition.

stories.title: MoMA to host exhibition on 1980s and 1990s design
stories.summary: The Museum of Modern Art will open Bold Is Better: ’80s and ’90s Design on January 17. The exhibition features 150 works spanning furniture, fashion, and technology. Curators aim to explore postmodern design narratives and the influence of popular culture during those two decades.

stories.title: Apple HomeView launch faces software and setup complaints
stories.summary: Early buyers of the $299 Apple HomeView are returning the devices due to setup failures and unreliable Siri performance. Reviewers have described the software as beta-like. Apple has promised a software update in December to address the issues, following years of market dominance by Google Home.

stories.title: Accessibility professionals address LLM-generated code
stories.summary: Disabled users are increasingly using LLM coding tools to create accessible apps and features. While some view this as an act of liberation, accessibility specialists note that the reality of these tools remains complicated. The trend highlights a growing reliance on AI for independent digital access.

stories.title: Creality introduces Falcon T1C laser engraver
stories.summary: Creality has launched the Falcon T1C, a compact laser engraver marketed toward small personalisation businesses. The company claims the device offers high-performance customisation for remote crafters. It joins a competitive market of budget-friendly laser cutters designed for adding unique designs to everyday products.

stories.title: BTR News reflects on amenity design
stories.summary: AGC BTR is examining the future of amenity design for build-to-rent residents. The publication provides industry reporting and property data to professionals in the sector. Access to the full report requires a free account registration on the platform.

stories.title: Suntory updates Maker’s Mark brand identity
stories.summary: Suntory Global Spirits is refreshing the Maker’s Mark brand with a new colour palette and typography based on the founder’s handwriting. The update includes new graphic elements focused on the brand's red wax seal. The design will roll out globally across retail and digital channels next year.

stories.title: Maker’s Mark reveals new handcrafted global identity by Turner Duckworth - Design Week
Maker’s Mark refreshes global brand identity
stories.summary: Maker’s Mark has revealed a refreshed visual identity, including new typography and photography. The update centres on the brand's signature red wax seal. The company says the design will appear across all global marketing channels, events, and experiences starting with the launch of its new website.

stories.title: The Points Guy unveils redesigned website
stories.summary: The Points Guy has launched a new brand identity and website as part of its evolution into a rewards intelligence platform. The site now features interactive tools and educational resources. The company aims to help consumers navigate the increasing complexity of loyalty programs and spending rewards.

stories.title: North Design rebrands Sainsbury Museum and Art Centre
stories.summary: North Design has created a new brand mark for the Sainsbury Museum and Art Centre, drawing inspiration from 1970s architectural sketches. The studio, which has previously worked with the Tate and Barbican, utilized geometric patterns to reflect the building's open-plan architecture.

stories.title: Maker’s Mark turns its signature red wax into a global design language - Ad Age
Pentagram refreshes Alpha Bank identity with ancient coin motif - Design Week
Woolworths rebrands WCafe as Woolies Café
stories.summary: Woolworths has rebranded its WCafe chain to Woolies Café, beginning with a flagship location at the V&A Waterfront. The company says the new concept is designed to integrate café visits into customers' daily routines. The move aims to position the brand as an accessible everyday destination.

stories.title: Pentagram rebrands Greece’s Alpha Bank around legacy symbol - Creative Review
The visual consistency of AI-generated posters
stories.summary: Generative AI posters frequently feature uncanny subjects and repetitive font choices. While these models are marketed as creative, their output often appears uniform. The issue stems from the underlying thinking models, which generate sequences of sub-prompts rather than original concepts.

stories.title: How to use reference images, video, and voice in Adobe Firefly to generate more consistent concept scenes - Softonic
OpenAI deploys agents for medical and insurance tasks
stories.summary: OpenAI is deploying GPT-6 Astra and Luna to act as digital clerks that navigate clinic programs and insurance portals. The company says the models handle administrative tasks reliably, with Luna costing about 8.5 cents per task. CVS Health is already using the agents for referrals.

stories.title: How to reframe one image for every channel with Adobe Firefly’s Generative Expand - Softonic
Adobe updates Premiere with AI-assisted color tools
stories.summary: Adobe Premiere 2027 includes new color tools intended to move beyond the Lumetri panel, which was based on the 2011 SpeedGrade engine. The company says the new features address the limitations of modern workflows. The update arrived last week at Adobe MAX.

stories.title: Canva adds text-to-image generation tools
stories.summary: Canva now offers Magic Media and Dream Lab to generate custom images from text prompts. The platform aims to allow users to create visuals without advanced graphic design skills. Results depend on the detail of the prompts and the user's editing choices.

stories.title: Adobe previews AI research projects at MAX Sneaks
stories.summary: Adobe showcased ten AI research projects at MAX Sneaks 2026, including tools for propagating editing decisions and manipulating canvas elements. The company describes these as laboratory promises rather than release dates. The prototypes anticipate the future direction of Photoshop and Premiere.

stories.title: Product design teams split on AI integration
stories.summary: Product design teams are divided on how to incorporate AI into their workflows. Some organizations are cautiously experimenting with the technology, while others have integrated it into daily tasks like research and coding. The shift reflects differing approaches to team organization and design processes.

stories.title: Accessibility testing lags behind AI-driven development
stories.summary: A report from Level Access suggests that while AI is accelerating software builds, accessibility testing practices have not kept pace. The study surveyed more than 2,500 professionals regarding the impact of AI on digital development. The build is moving faster than the checks.

stories.title: Anthropic Just Released New Rules of Claude Code
stories.summary: Things move fast in the AI space, and what we considered best practices for Claude Code just a few months ago may already be outdated with… Continue reading on UX Planet »

stories.title: MaPC app enables Windows gaming on Mac
stories.summary: MaPC launched in mid-October as a free app that runs Windows games on Apple Silicon using Wine, DXVK, and MoltenVK. The software automates setup for Steam, Epic, and GOG titles. In its first month, the developer shipped 32 versions of the tool.

stories.title: Lamm and Kirch design 2026 book catalog
stories.summary: Designer Florian Lamm created the catalog for the Best Book Design from All over the World 2026. The publication features no horizontal cover title, instead stacking upright capitals along the fore-edge. The design pairs OT Scholar type with photos by Attila Hartwig.

stories.title: Jev can 10x your Claude Code
stories.summary: Jev is a new AI model from a co-inventor of ChatGPT, and this model has created a lot of buzz in the product design & development space… Continue reading on UX Planet »

stories.title: Claude expands interactive app connectors
stories.summary: Claude is updating its interface to allow connected apps to open alongside chats or in full screen. Using the open MCP Apps standard, the platform enables users to modify files and rows directly. The rollout is gradual and requires specific account access.

stories.title: Figma data highlights Australian AI adoption
stories.summary: Figma research indicates that Australian organizations are currently ahead of the global average for AI adoption and team collaboration. A survey of local professionals suggests that as AI use expands, teams are facing new bottlenecks related to quality, alignment, and judgment.

stories.title: Election Commission warns of NID fraud
stories.summary: The Election Commission has warned citizens against fraudsters offering National Identity card corrections via social media. The commission stated that scammers are impersonating officials to collect money. The agency clarified that it does not provide correction services through platforms like WhatsApp or Facebook Messenger.

stories.title: Anant Anadi Vadnagar Museum Wins Red Dot Best of the Best 2026 - CMO Gujarat
NID students place at Maruti Suzuki DesignXathon
stories.summary: Students from the National Institute of Design secured the top two runner-up positions at the second Maruti Suzuki DesignXathon. The competition challenged over 450 participants from 70 institutes to envision an iconic vehicle for Gen Z and Gen Alpha to own in 2036. The future is currently being sketched.

stories.title: India's First Museum To Win The Red Dot 'Best Of The Best' Is Built Around Ancient Ruins - NDTV
Vadnagar museum receives Red Dot award
stories.summary: The Anant Anadi Vadnagar-Archaeological Experiential Museum has been awarded the Red Dot Best of the Best Award 2026 in Berlin. Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghvi noted the museum is the first in India to receive the honor. The site is now officially a global destination for history.

stories.title: SECI adopts new logo
stories.summary: Solar Energy Corporation of India has introduced a new logo featuring rotating forms inspired by turbine blades. Designed by NID Ahmedabad, the visual identity marks the next phase of the organization as it expands its renewable energy mandate. The logo will be adopted across all platforms progressively.

stories.title: Court bars Blinkit from using fan likeness
stories.summary: The Madras High Court has issued an interim order barring Blinkit from using the image of Chennai Super Kings superfan Saravanan Hari without his consent. The fan is seeking 1.1 crore rupees in damages, alleging the platform used his likeness to imply an endorsement. Personality rights remain a legal consideration.

stories.title: SECI updates branding with new tagline
stories.summary: Solar Energy Corporation of India has unveiled a new logo and the tagline Energy Forever, For All. Designed by the National Institute of Design, the branding reflects the organization's expanding renewable energy mandate. The company is now officially committed to the future in writing.

stories.title: Fermat raises 8 million dollars for AI fashion platform
stories.summary: Barcelona-based Fermat has raised 8 million dollars in seed funding to open a New York office and expand its software into garment production. The company claims to have tripled its revenue this year. It did not disclose specific revenue figures or a valuation for the AI design tool.

stories.title: Daydream launches AI stylist agent
stories.summary: Fashion startup Daydream has launched an AI agent designed to act as a personal stylist. The company says the tool can help users plan looks, virtually try on clothes, and shop. The goal is to put a personal stylist in everyone's pocket, provided the pocket is digital.

stories.title: Voyage Labs raises 12 million dollars for travel AI
stories.summary: Voyage Labs has raised 12 million dollars in seed funding for Atlas, a specialized AI travel-planning assistant. The startup is betting that a dedicated agent can outperform general-purpose models. The funding will be used to grow the engineering team and expand supplier partnerships for future trips.

stories.title: Lumov in talks for 33 crore rupee funding
stories.summary: Orthopaedic products brand Lumov is reportedly in talks to raise 33 crore rupees in a round led by Peak XV's Surge programme. The startup manufactures braces for post-surgical recovery and pain management. Neither the company nor the investor responded to requests for comment regarding the potential deal.

stories.title: Fermat expands AI fashion software
stories.summary: Fermat has raised 8 million dollars to open a New York office and launch Techpacks, a tool for turning designs into factory-ready specifications. The company says it is evolving from a design tool into a full garment production platform. The software is currently used by over 350 customers.

stories.title: Tiberius Aerospace reaches unicorn status
stories.summary: Tiberius Aerospace has raised 85 million dollars in a Series A round, pushing its valuation above 1 billion dollars. The startup designs AI-powered munitions to address manufacturing bottlenecks in defense. It achieved unicorn status 14 months after closing a 4.5 million dollar seed round.

stories.title: Fermat secures 7.26 million euro seed round
stories.summary: Fermat has raised 7.26 million euros to expand its AI fashion platform. Investor Kibo Ventures cited explosive growth and near-zero customer churn as reasons for the investment. The company plans to use the capital to open a New York office and scale its garment production software.

stories.title: Fermat raises $8M to bridge the gap between fashion designers and manufacturers - Tech.eu
Fermat raises 8 million dollars for fashion tech
stories.summary: AI fashion platform Fermat has raised 8 million dollars in seed funding to expand into garment production. The company, which launched in 2022, is introducing a tool to create factory-ready specifications. It claims to have more than 350 customers, including Asos and New Look.

stories.title: UNOPS seeks communications officer
stories.summary: The United Nations Office for Project Services is hiring a communications officer to support the United Nations Youth Office. The role is home-based and focuses on graphic design, social media management, and visual storytelling. The organization is looking for someone to amplify the voices of young people.

stories.title: MICA student reflects on design education
stories.summary: Rhythm Singhal, a student from India, credits the community at MICA for her growth as an artist. She notes that the institution's sense of inclusivity guided her decision to study abroad. The power of design is described as being found in more than just form and function.

stories.title: Cedarville University highlights industrial design program
stories.summary: Cedarville University offers an industrial design program that splits time between its campus and the International Center for Creativity. Graduates have designed products for companies including Chick-fil-A and Bose. The program is currently marketed as the only evangelical industrial design course in the nation.

stories.title: Dezeen launches 20x20 project
stories.summary: To celebrate its 20th birthday, Dezeen has launched a project in partnership with Kohler. The series asks 20 established architects and designers to select one peer they believe will have the biggest impact over the next 20 years. The future is currently being scheduled in four-week increments.

stories.title: Bjarke Ingels selects Harry Nuriev for 20x20
stories.summary: Bjarke Ingels has selected Harry Nuriev as a designer likely to influence the next 20 years. Nuriev founded Crosby Studios 12 years ago, basing his practice on a game of rejection where he avoids materials and colours that he believes are currently popular with others.

stories.title: Saskatchewan designer wins WorldSkills silver
stories.summary: Saskatchewan Polytechnic graduate Jorda Thomas earned a silver medal and Best of Nation honours in graphic design at the WorldSkills competition in Shanghai. The result marks the first time a competitor from Saskatchewan has reached the podium at the international event. She was not expecting it.

stories.title: TIAT gallery showcases experimental tech
stories.summary: The Intersection of Art and Technology is a gallery in San Francisco featuring devices like a frog-shaped computer and an AI assistant inside a fuzzy parrot. The space aims to get people to love technology again by displaying hardware that does not resemble standard consumer electronics.

stories.title: Google designer on working across borders
stories.summary: Google senior UX designer Yi Xiang discusses his career and the lessons learned from working in different cultures. After moving between countries, he concluded that cultural differences are indeed a thing. He previously believed that people were the same everywhere.

stories.title: Ines Launay on her illustration process
stories.summary: French illustrator Ines Launay creates colourful compositions using inspiration from trail running, wooden toys and textile crafts. Her portfolio features loose pencil marks and wonky characters. She keeps foam and polka dots close at hand while working.

research.title: Developing JEEVHITAA: Designing and Evaluating a Human-Centered AI Ecosystem for Collective Care
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Health management is often a collective activity, involving family members and close relations in monitoring, interpreting, and coordinating care. Yet, most digital health technologies remain individual-centric, offering limited support for the distributed responsibilities and negotiated information. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Development of an HPLC Analytical Method Based on Large Language Models:A Case Study of the Eczema External Wash Formula
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas feature complex chemical compositions, and their HPLC quality control method development is time-consuming and experience-dependent. Large language models (LLMs) provide a promising strategy for intelligently assisting analytical method construction. Taking the. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: From XR Sketches to CAD: Preserving Design Intent with AI
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Extended reality (XR) allows designers to sketch shapes directly in 3D, but converting these sketches into editable, feature-based CAD requires interpreting their intent. A sketch may contain drawing errors, intended features, and design choices that remain. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: LLM Facilitation of Group Decision-Making
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Human groups often fail to integrate information distributed across their members, converging on incorrect decisions. We ask whether large language models (LLMs) can help groups reach the correct decision in such settings. In an online, chat-based. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: MemoryLane: Supporting Reminiscence Conversations Between Older Adults with Mild Dementia and Lay Caregivers Using a Simulated AI Agent
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Reminiscence Therapy (RT) is a non-pharmacological intervention that invites patients to discuss and review past life experiences and memories to improve their emotional and mental well-being. In practice, many reminiscence conversations are led by lay caregivers. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: PromptPoseFX: Authoring Pose-Driven Visual Effects through Augmented Prompting and Interactive Refinement
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Human pose-driven visual effects offer a compelling way for enhancing video expressiveness and storytelling. Authoring such effects with traditional video editing tools is a complex and time-consuming task that requires considerable technical expertise and manual effort. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
research.summary: Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the.

research.title: Reveal: A Provenance-Aware System for Multimodal Urban Data Exploration
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Urban sensing initiatives increasingly produce multimodal datasets that combine visual and textual information to capture city characteristics and subjective factors such as safety, comfort, and accessibility. Yet, analyzing such data at scale remains difficult, as manual. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
